task: The B-8db9 hotfix proved single-story review structurally cannot catch cross-story interaction defects — B-cf60 and B-4b22 each passed review but combined into a CRITICAL gate bypass on main. There is no written process rule telling maintainers to run a combination review after merging parallel process-framework stories; the lesson currently lives only in conversation.
outcome: A reader opening CLAUDE.md finds a new short subsection (near the REVIEW / 对抗审查 area) titled something like 「合并态组合审查（流程框架并行 story）」 that states: when multiple process-framework stories touching classifier / gate policy / command entry guards / auto-commit / DONE merge semantics merge to main in parallel, a read-only combination review must be run over the combined main state, checking classification priority order, gate policy, command entry rejection, auto-commit/dirty state, and DONE merge semantics for cross-story conflicts. The same rule is reflected in docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md. The rule explicitly scopes to process-framework stories only and is advisory discipline, not a CLI gate.
facts: B-8db9 hotfix (2026-05-15) fixed a CRITICAL bypass formed by B-cf60 + B-4b22 only after both merged to main
Each of B-cf60 and B-4b22 passed its own single-story REVIEW independently
CLAUDE.md already has a 对抗审查 section and REVIEW-phase rules — the new rule fits as a sibling subsection
This is a doc-only change — no code, no new CLI command, no gate
constraints: Doc-only change: edit CLAUDE.md and/or docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md; touch no code
Rule is advisory process discipline — explicitly NOT a new CLI gate and NOT auto-enforced
Rule scoped to process-framework stories (classifier / gate policy / command entry guards / auto-commit / DONE merge semantics) — must not impose combination review on ordinary business stories
The rule text must name the concrete checklist of what a combination review inspects, so it is actionable not vague
Cite B-8db9 as the originating incident so future readers can trace why the rule exists
